one_liner: HubSpot is ready for an agent toolkit, with a publicly documented CRM API, free development access, and a vendor-operated MCP server.

auth.notes: OAuth is required for apps installed across multiple accounts. Static access tokens support single-account installation; some app features require a developer API key.

access.notes: A free account provides a route to app credentials and API use. Installation depends on the installing user's permissions; marketplace listing involves review, and free accounts have API rate limits.

api.notes: The memo describes a public REST reference covering CRM, marketing, conversations, files, and other areas, plus an HTTP GraphQL endpoint.

mcp.notes: HubSpot documents a CRM MCP server and a developer-platform MCP server. The memo does not assign a specific MCP tool breadth.

verdict.rationale: Free CRM access, obtainable app credentials, and documented API use provide a development path. The contacts API supports creating and managing records, and OAuth supports apps installed across accounts.

evidence.quote: “There are two authentication types available based on how you plan to distribute your app: OAuth is required for multiple accounts, while static auth access tokens are used for installing in a single account at a time.”
“Some app features and settings require a developer API key, which is available in the developer overview of your HubSpot account.”
“And unlike a free trial, it's 100% free with no expiration date. Get free CRM No credit card required.”

“Under Client credentials , copy the Client ID and Client secret from your new app and paste them into the corresponding locations in your OAuth server’s configuration, then restart your OAuth server.”
“Privately distributed apps (Any Hub) Free and Starter 100 / app 250,000 / account”
“All APIs, whether legacy, new, or beta, use the same root path as before: https://api.hubapi.com/ .”
“The contacts endpoints allow you to create and manage contact records in your HubSpot account, as well as sync contact data between HubSpot and other systems.”

“In addition to using GraphQL in your website pages , you can also use a GraphQL query in your integration, a Jamstack site , or in a custom code action in the workflows tool to specify the data you need from HubSpot without having to make separate requests to multiple API endpoints.”
“HubSpot offers two distinct MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers — one for connecting any MCP-compatible AI tool or agent to your CRM, and one for building on the HubSpot Developer Platform.”
“HubSpot MCP Server for Claude and Cursor Hosted HubSpot MCP for Claude, Cursor, and ChatGPT. Manage contacts, deals, and tickets in bulk, with managed OAuth or a direct API key.”

problems: A few attempted documentation and pricing URLs did not load directly; accessible official pages supplied the evidence above.
The MCP overview contains differing descriptions of its current read/write capabilities, so this memo does not assign a specific MCP tool breadth.
name: HubSpot

verification.note: The quotes establish OAuth, static access tokens, and a developer API key. OAuth is required for apps distributed across multiple accounts.

The quotes show a free account, instructions for obtaining app credentials, and API limits for apps on the Free tier. The notes about installation permissions and marketplace review are not evidenced.
The API root and contacts endpoints support the REST claim, and the GraphQL quote explicitly describes integration use. The quotes do not establish the notes' list of additional API areas.
HubSpot's own page says it offers two MCP servers.
The quote is from a Composio page for a HubSpot toolkit.
Self-serve free access and a documented API with contact creation and management support buildable_now with no identified blocker.
